message.content: {"verdict": "not_supported", "passage": 1, "reason": "The source states the opposite: on delayed tests including one week, prior testing produced substantially greater retention than studying, with repeated studying beating testing only at the 5-minute delay (passage 2)."}
message.reasoning_content:
The claim: "Repeated studying produced better recall than repeated testing on the final test given one week later."

Passage [2]: "When the final test was given after 5 min, repeated studying improved recall relative to repeated testing." — This is for the 5 min delay, not one week later.

Passage [1]: "on the delayed tests, prior testing produced substantially greater retention than studying" — This contradicts the claim for delayed tests (2 days, 1 week). At one week, testing was better than studying.

So the claim says studying better than testing at one week — the source says the opposite: testing better than studying on delayed tests including one week. Passage [2] supports studying better only at 5 min.

So verdict: not_supported. The claim contradicts passage [1] (testing produced greater retention on delayed tests) and passage [2] only supports the 5-min condition, not one week.

Which passage to cite? Passage [1] directly contradicts: on delayed tests (including 1 week), testing > studying. So verdict not_supported, passage 1.

Reason: The source states the opposite—prior testing produced greater retention than studying on delayed tests including one week—while studying only beat testing at the 5-minute delay.
